consejos_sinergias: Vitamins D, E, K and omega-3s are absorbed better when taken with the day's meal with the most healthy fat (never on an empty stomach).

Most of your iron comes from plant sources (non-heme), which absorb less well: combine lentils/spinach with a vitamin C source in the same meal (red pepper, lemon, kiwi) — it can multiply absorption 3-6x.
Keep coffee or tea at least 1-2 hours away from your main iron-rich meals: tannins significantly reduce iron absorption.
Combining legumes with egg or dairy in the same meal improves how well your body can use the zinc and iron.
You asked for an anti-inflammatory approach: this plan leans on olive oil, avocado, nuts/seeds, and deeply colored vegetables and fruit.
Given the stress/sleep you reported, this plan leans on magnesium-rich sources (legumes, nuts, seeds, quinoa).
With a mostly sedentary job, this plan leans on higher-fiber sources (legumes, oats, whole grains, vegetables) to help with satiety and digestion.
advertencias_revision_humana: The client hasn't attached bloodwork, but there's a relevant unverified note: "Client mentions feeling tired frequently lately. Hasn't provided bloodwork yet; still need to ask for it at follow-up." — ask for it at follow-up so the diet can be modulated with real data.
mensaje_para_el_cliente: Hi Javier, here's your draft diet. No food is banned in this approach — amounts and context do the work. Judge it by whether you could still be doing this in three months, not whether it's perfect today. Anything that clashes with your day-to-day, let me know and we'll trade it for something equivalent.
